paper.title: Gated Knowledge-Guided Prototype Transfer for Zero-Support Medical Vision Language Model
paper.authors: Sumaiya Fazal, Rizwan Qureshi, Laleh Behjat, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou
paper.affiliation: FAST-NUCES · MGH/Harvard · University of Calgary · Mila

inputs.classes: No DR (3), Mild (1), Moderate (1), Severe (0), Proliferative (0)

tiles.label: Negative-transfer rate
tiles.sub: share of 50 support draws where missing-class recall fell; ungated (VLM / ontology) → gated

figures.title: How often does borrowing knowledge make the missing classes worse?
figures.caption: Each dot is one random support draw (same support for all methods). Orange dots: missing-class recall fell relative to SS-Text+ (negative transfer). Black bar = mean. Dotted line = −5 points (severe negative transfer).

figures.title: Is the gate just a smaller step size?
figures.caption: Same hybrid neighbours, transfer strength β varied. Ungated uses the full β; gated uses β·g with g from the evidence (agreement × relevance). Dotted line = your β. Extension, not in the paper.

figures.title: Gate inspector: why each zero-support class gets the update it gets
figures.caption: Agreement a = how much the selected residuals point the same way; relevance q = √(VLM margin × 1/ontology distance). Orange ticks: the paper's MESSIDOR gates.

figures.title: Who pays, who gains? Recall per class
figures.caption: Mean recall over support draws. Shaded = zero-support classes. Paper (MESSIDOR), severe / proliferative recall: gated 46.53 / 73.71 vs KGPT-VLM 37.47 / 68.00.

compare.metric: SS-Text+ Top-1 / ACA / MCR / SCR / H
compare.note: absolute levels depend on the synthetic world
NTR = share of draws with ΔMCR < 0; severe = ΔMCR < −5
